# Test-only Source Map contract fixtures

**Nothing in this directory is real evidence.** Every document is synthetic, and every
Persian narrative line is written about the fixture itself rather than about any real video
or post. No report, answer, or UI may present this content as knowledge extracted from a
source.

Delivered by `T-251`, against [`schemas/synthesis/v1/`](../../../schemas/synthesis/v1/README.md).

## What is here

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `valid/youtube-source_knowledge.json` | A `PASS` brief over `tests/fixtures/runs/pass-run` |
| `valid/twitter-source_knowledge.json` | A `PASS` brief over `tests/fixtures/twitter-runs/quote` |
| `valid/partial-source_knowledge.json` | A `PARTIAL` brief over `tests/fixtures/runs/partial-run` |
| `valid/synthesis/source_relations.json` | The container, holding one qualified YouTube↔X relation |
| `valid/synthesis/source_relations.empty.json` | A pass that compared a pair and emitted nothing |
| `valid/synthesis/source_relations.bounded.json` | A pass that hit its candidate bound and counted the omissions |
| `invalid/*.json` | One document per lie, each with a `*.note.json` sidecar naming it |

The two media are the point of the valid set. `T-228` proved YouTube and X coexist through
every read surface; these prove the source-level contract is written once for both, with the
same brief shape over a time-based medium and a text-based one, and a relation whose two
endpoints are of different media.

## Why they are generated

`build_fixtures.py` reads the committed runs and takes their **real** unit ids and their
**real** input digests, through `x2knwldg.synthesis` — the same function the `T-252` and
`T-253` apply gates will use. A hand-written brief whose `based_on` named `KU-000007` would
look exactly like a valid one and would pin nothing: the schema cannot see the run, and a
test reading the fixture would simply agree with it.

```bash
.venv/bin/python tests/fixtures/source-map/build_fixtures.py
git status --porcelain -- tests/fixtures/source-map/   # expect: empty
```

Regeneration is byte-identical, which is why nothing here takes a timestamp from the clock.

## The invalid catalogue is the load-bearing half

A schema that rejects nothing promises nothing. Each invalid document tells exactly **one**
lie, and its sidecar records which of two things refuses it:

- **`schema`** — `schemas/synthesis/v1/` alone refuses it.
- **`gate`** — it needs a second document in hand (the run's own unit list, its
  `validation.json`, the other endpoint's units) and is therefore a rule for the `T-252` /
  `T-253` apply gates. The fixture exists now so those gates are written against a committed
  case rather than against a description of one.

`tests/test_source_map_schemas.py` checks the *claim*, not just the document: a case filed
under `schema` that the schema in fact accepts fails the suite, because a contract whose
README overstates what it refuses is worse than one that refuses less and says so.

The notes live in sidecars rather than inside the documents because every schema here sets
`additionalProperties: false` — a `_fixture_note` key would make the record invalid for the
wrong reason, and the fixture would stop testing what it was written to test.

## What these fixtures deliberately are not

They are **not** written into the runs they cite. `tests/fixtures/runs/` and
`tests/fixtures/twitter-runs/` are regenerated by their own generators, which do not produce
a `source_knowledge.json`; adding one by hand would break the byte-identical regeneration
check in `PROJECT_MANAGEMENT.md` §7.2 and move the runs' subtree digests. When `T-252` gives
the pipeline a gate that writes the artifact into a run, that generator can produce it and
these documents become the contract cases they already are.

No book, PDF, EPUB, Medium or web fixture appears here. Those sources have no capture
contract, and a fixture is not a source of support.
